newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-ROBINS WINS LEICESTER LEAGUE CUP SEMIFINAL BERTH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ROBINS WINS LEICESTER LEAGUE CUP SEMIFINAL BERTH.

text.p: Former Manchester United striker Mark Robins scored the only goal of the match to earn premier league Leicester a League Cup semifinal berth as they held off a spirited challenge by first division Ipswich on Tuesday.
Robins, 27, making only his fourth start of the season, hit a goal of sheer class just before the interval, unleashing a tremendous 25-metre drive into the corner of the Ipswich net.

Ipswich mounted a series of attacks in the opening 20 minutes of the second half but the Leicester defence held fast before returning to the attack themselves and in the end deserved the win which earned them a semifinal against Wimbledon who were also in action on Tuesday, winning their F.A. Cup third replay 2-0 against second division Crewe.
A goal in each half from Robbie Earle and Dean Holdsworth secured the London club a fourth-round match at Manchester United.

But it was an unconvincing performance by Wimbledon in front of a home crowd of only 4,951 on a bitterly cold night. The London club took the lead when Crewe midfielder Peter Billing miskicked the ball straight into the path of Earle whose volley rocketed into the net.
Wimbledon made the match secure immediately within a minute of the start of the second half when Oyvind Leonhardsen sent in a low cross which Holdsworth turned into the net.

Second division Gillingham's hopes of further F.A. Cup glory were ended by struggling premier league Derby who clinched a 2-0 victory through strikes by their Dutch pair Ron Willems and Robin van der Laan who both scored in the second half to end Derby's run of seven matches without a win.
In the fourth round, Derby will play either Aston Villa or Notts County who meet in a third-round replay on Wednesday.

A spirited second-half revival by Luton deservedly kept them in the F.A .Cup, although they had to wait until nearly three minutes into stoppage time before getting the equaliser, scrambled home by defender Marvin Johnson following a corner with almost every player trying to make contact with the ball.
Bolton had taken the lead in the 26th minute when Nathan Blake broke clear to set up Jamie Pollock for his first goal of the season.
Watford won through to the fourth round with a 2-0 win against Oxford with late goals by both strikers Devon White and David Connolly in a match which the fates seemed to have conspired to prevent.

The first attempt to play the tie last week was called off a minute before it was due to start because of bad weather and on Tuesday the kick-off was delayed for 45 minutes when the floodlights failed.

White finally opened the scoring after 71 minutes with a fine piece of individual play when he rounded a defender before beating goalkeeper Phil Whitehead and nine minutes later Connolly made their fourth-round place secure when he fired a low drive into the net.
